Cc: none
Subject: Vantorre CX-10 refurbished combi

We paid $14,800 inc GST for this refurbished Vantorre CX-10, delivered and commissioned on 14 September with a six-month parts and labour warranty. The listing said the steam generator had been descaled and pressure tested.

On 22 September, Kelsall attended for E34, a steam generator low-water-level fault causing intermittent lockouts in steam and combi modes. The service report recorded nine E34 errors since delivery and an inlet pressure of 320 kPa, which the technician recorded as OK. He replaced the water level sensor under warranty and tested three steam cycles.

E34 returned four times the following week. We also reported the core probe reading 63°C against 70°C on our Thermapen in a lamb shoulder, with the same result on a repeat test. On 6 October, the technician found the generator heavily scaled, descaled and flushed it, and recalibrated the probe to within one degree.

Kelsall recommended a water softener, saying the scale indicated hard water. I checked with the water company: Fitzroy’s average supply hardness is about 15 mg/L as CaCO3, which they described as soft. The oven had been on our water for only three weeks when the heavy scale was found. We can’t establish when it built up, but we don’t think the site-water explanation has been established.

On Saturday 24 October, E34 locked us out at 6.10 pm with 60 covers booked. We finished the lamb on the stove and in the deck oven, took pork belly off the menu and absorbed the cost. Kelsall reported E34 and further scale at its 27 October visit. Brett has since said this was a site-water issue outside warranty and advised a $280 callout plus GST.

For a unit around six weeks old and sold with a parts and labour warranty, we don’t think that charge is reasonable. Other kitchens should have these details before spending nearly $15,000.
